newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOECHST, CLARIANT MERGE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS.
newsitem.headline: HOECHST, CLARIANT MERGE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Tuesday it will merge its specialty chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG , in a bid to overcome conditions in the sector.
Hoechst said it will take a sizeable minority stake in Clariant, adding the new merged specialty chemicals group will post annual sales of nine billion marks.
In a statement Hoechst said the step reflected the difficult situation in its own specialty chemicals unit.

Hoechst said it would contribute its speciality chemicals business, masterbatches (which are tailored plastic resins), pigments, additives, auxilliaries including textile and leather chemicals, fine chemicals, dispersions and cellulose ethers.
A Hoechst spokeswoman said the supervisory board had not yet agreed to the merger but expected to receive news this afternoon.

Hoechst said Clariant would remain a Swiss share company, indicating that Hoechst would effectively receive a share market quotation for these products and thus increase shareholder value for the parent company.

The merger will result in a larger product portfolio as well as an improved geographical presence and new growth opportunities. Both companies look to gain savings totalling several hundred million Swiss francs from the deal.
A Clariant spokesman queried by Reuters said the Swiss group expected to make a statement later in the day, probably after 2:00 p.m. (1300 GMT). "We have no comment for the moment."
Clariant is one of the world's leading manufacturers of textile dyes and chemicals. It also produces dyes and chemicals for leather, paper and plastics.

Clariant was spun off as a specialty chemicals unit by Sandoz AG last year as part of Sandoz's concentration on pharmaceuticals and nutrition ahead of its planned merger with Ciba-Geigy AG as the new firm Novartis AG.
Shares in Clariant were suspended from trading on the Swiss Exchange on Tuesday at the company's request, an exchange spokeswoman said.
She added the shares would be suspended until further notice from the company and it was not clear when this would happen.

Registered shares in Clariant were suspended around 1104 GMT and were last traded at 459 Swiss francs, up 11 francs from Monday's close. Trading volume in Clariant was relatively heavy with 32,518 shares traded.
